problem_type: model picker ordering and provider identity are duplicated across entry points
symptom: The same model can appear once per provider, and a user preference cannot consistently control which configured provider is selected first.
direct_cause: Catalog options were consumed as flat rows by several pickers, while provider availability and ordering were not represented in one shared view-model.
class_root: Provider identity, configuration state, and ordering are cross-surface semantics. Keeping them in individual pickers guarantees drift between generation nodes, storyboard rows, batch controls, and the Agent composer.
affected_population: Users with the same model available through two or more providers
Users who have connected providers alongside unconfigured catalog entries
Every model selection surface that previously consumed flat catalog options
entry_points: Canvas and storyboard batch model pickers
internal_only_reason: The catalog, settings bridge, and renderer pickers are internal Nomi contracts.
invariants: Every picker uses the canonical identity aggregation and shared provider sorting function.
A configured provider is always before an unconfigured provider; saved preference breaks configured ties and all remaining ties are stable.
Selecting a model row uses the first configured provider; selecting a provider chip writes the exact provider and model identity.
Unconfigured providers remain visible, are grouped and dimmed, and route to model setup without silently generating.
Preference writes use schema version 1, atomic JSON persistence, and trusted sender validation.
generality_proof: The shared hook is consumed by stateful generation, storyboard, and Agent pickers, while the shared batch picker covers both batch entry points; a single identity and ordering boundary therefore covers every current caller.

shared_boundaries.responsibility: Own canonical model grouping, configured-state ordering, preference ordering, and stable tie-breaking.
Own the versioned cross-process settings shape and input normalization.

same_class_entry_points.evidence: Unit tests cover deduplication, preferred ordering, unconfigured grouping, and stable sorting.
Both canvas and storyboard batch callers pass through the same component and shared ordering input.
The composer adapts catalog rows into the shared hook and uses the same provider chip callback.

migration: No existing model identity is rewritten. Catalog rows are grouped at read time by canonical model key; the new version-1 preference document is created atomically on first save and an absent or invalid document normalizes to an empty order.

recurrence.reason: This is the first implementation of the provider preference boundary; regression coverage records the shared boundary without introducing a separate structural gate.
same_class_scan: rg modelOptionMappers, vendorKey, ModelSelect, useDedupedModelSelect, and BulkModelPicker across src and electron
Documented all current model picker entry points in docs/qa/2026-09-06-vendor-order-design-lab.md

legacy_paths.rationale: No parallel provider ordering implementation is retained; existing picker callers converge on the shared boundary.

residual_risks: The first phase does not automatically retry or switch providers during generation; that remains phase two.
The real-provider generation step in the journey requires the fixture response path and must never be mistaken for live provider certification.
